cards.text: Joshua, Israel's leader, is near the city of Jericho when he looks up. A man is standing right in front of him, holding a drawn sword. Me? I'd have hopped my gold base straight back to the bakery.

cards.question: Joshua doesn't run. He walks right up to the man with the sword. What does Joshua ask Him?

answers.text: Are You for us or for our enemies
Have You come out from Jericho
What is Your name and Your people

cards.question: When Joshua asks whose side He's on, the man with the sword says He's on Israel's side.
The man with the sword answers Joshua, “Neither.” So who does He say He is?

cards.text: Joshua hits the ground facedown in reverence. Then he asks, “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?”

cards.question: The Commander of the LORD's army tells Joshua the place where he's standing is holy. So what does He tell Joshua to do?

cards.text: And Joshua does it, right there. Now, friend, take a look at the city.

cards.question: With the Israelites close by, Jericho keeps its gates open, and people come and go like normal.

cards.text: No one goes out, and no one comes in. Jericho is shut up tighter than the junk drawer I spent all those years in. Then the LORD speaks to Joshua.

cards.question: Before anybody marches anywhere, the LORD tells Joshua He has delivered Jericho into Joshua's hand.

cards.text: The city, its king and its mighty men of valor, all of it in Joshua's hand. Now, friend, get ready for the battle plan.

cards.question: Step one of the LORD's plan: all the men of war circle Jericho ___ time each day, for six days.

cards.text: And here's who leads the way: seven priests carrying seven rams' horns, walking in front of the ark.

cards.question: Six days of marching, one lap around Jericho a day. What's different on the seventh day?

answers.text: They circle the city seven times
They circle the city one last time
They camp and wait at the gates

cards.question: When the priests give a long blast on the ram's horn, the people give a mighty ___, and the city's ___ will collapse.

cards.text: Then all the people charge straight into the city. Friend, I've got cookie recipes with more steps than that battle plan.
So Joshua son of Nun calls the priests and passes the plan along. Out they go, seven priests blowing seven rams' horns, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD following them.

cards.question: Armed troops march out front, then the priests with their horns, then the ark. Who brings up the back of the line?

cards.text: But Joshua gave the people one more order. And friend, this one would've been the hardest one for me.

cards.question: The horns keep sounding as they march. What's Joshua's order for the people?

answers.text: Not one word until he says shout
Sing praises the whole way around
Call on the city to surrender

cards.text: Not one word until Joshua says, “Then you are to shout!” Friend, I can't make one lap around my own oven without talking to the cookies.

cards.question: After circling Jericho once, the people head back to the camp and spend the night there.

cards.text: The next morning, Joshua is up early, and the priests take up the ark of the LORD again.

cards.question: On the second day, the priests stop blowing the horns so the march around Jericho is totally silent.

cards.text: Horns sounding, one lap, back to camp. Six days of that, and I'd have been the guy on day four mouthing, “Is this the day? Is THIS the day?”

cards.question: On the seventh day, they get up at ___ and march around Jericho seven times.

cards.text: That's the only day they go around seven times. After the seventh lap, the priests blow the horns, and Joshua finally opens his mouth.

cards.question: Seven laps done, the horns blowing. What does Joshua command the people?

answers.text: Shout for the LORD has given you the city
Stand back and watch the wall fall
Charge in before the gates can open

cards.text: Joshua isn't done talking yet. The city and everything in it must be devoted to the LORD for destruction, except for one house.

cards.question: Only one household in Jericho will live. Whose?

answers.text: Rahab and all those with her
Tamar and all those with her
Deborah and all those with her

cards.question: Joshua says Rahab the prostitute gets spared because she ___ the spies Israel sent.

cards.text: Then a warning. Keep away from the things devoted to destruction, or you'll bring disaster on the whole camp of Israel.

cards.question: Joshua tells the soldiers they can keep any silver and gold they find in Jericho.

cards.text: All of it is holy to the LORD and goes into His treasury. Then the horns sound, the people give a great shout, and the wall COLLAPSES.
All the people charge straight into the city and capture it. With the sword, they devote everything in it to destruction, people and animals alike.

cards.question: Joshua sends someone into Rahab's house to bring her out. Who does he send?

answers.text: The two men who spied out the land
The seven priests with the horns
The rear guard behind the ark

cards.text: Just as they promised, the spies bring out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers and her whole family. Friend, that's a promise kept better than the expired coupon I shared a drawer with ever kept one.

cards.question: The spies settle Rahab's family inside the camp of Israel.

cards.text: Then the Israelites burn the city and everything in it. But the silver, gold, bronze and iron go into the treasury of the LORD's house.

cards.question: Joshua spares Rahab and her family, and she goes on living among the ___.

cards.text: Then Joshua makes a solemn oath about Jericho, and it's about whoever would try to build it again.

cards.question: What does Joshua's oath say about the man who rises up and rebuilds Jericho?

answers.text: He is cursed before the LORD
He is blessed with a great name
He will rule over all the land

cards.question: The LORD is with Joshua, and his fame spreads throughout the land.

cards.text: And that's where we leave Jericho for now. Hang on to your apron, friend, because Israel's story in this land isn't done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "Is this the day? Is THIS the day?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank sits before the singular word "time" ("circle Jericho ___ time each day"). Only "one" fits the grammar. "three time" and "seven time" sound broken, so the right answer stands out by grammar, not by reasoning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They circle the city one last time" can be argued as right. The seventh day is the last day they circle the city (Joshua 6:4, 6:15). A baker could read "one last time" as "for the last time" and say it describes the seventh day.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Joshua finally opens his mouth" says Joshua had been silent until the seventh day. The text shows him speaking before the march: he gives orders to the priests and the people (Joshua 6:6-7, 6:10). The order to stay silent was for the people, not for Joshua.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The right answer is Joshua's own command ("Shout for the LORD has given you the city"). It is longer than the other two and is the only one that sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers are short, plain lines ("Stand back and watch the wall fall", "Charge in before the gates can open").

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke laughs at one of Papa Dorin's friends from the drawer, the expired coupon, by saying it never kept a promise. It doesn't laugh at himself. It also cuts against how fondly he remembers the coupon "that never stopped believing."

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.

findings.problem: Joshua's oath in Joshua 6:26 includes the price of rebuilding Jericho: it costs the builder his firstborn for the foundations and his youngest for the gates. No card tells this. Cards 13 and 14 only say the man who rebuilds the city is cursed, so the baker misses an important detail of the oath.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
